_about.table: the distribution kernel table: the kernel a fresh install of the current stable release gives on first boot, never a backport
_about.fields: Name, Base, Kernel, Approx (true when the kernel was not checked against the release notes), Policy, NvidiaEasy, Newcomer (1 to 5), Note, Source, Verified
_about.warning: goes stale faster than anything else; the scanner warns when Verified is over 120 days old

Distros.Name: Linux Mint
Distros.Policy: Pinned to the Ubuntu LTS kernel; newer kernels available in Update Manager but not installed by default.
Distros.Note: The standard recommendation for someone leaving Windows. Familiar desktop, conservative, NVIDIA driver manager built in.

Distros.Name: Ubuntu LTS
Distros.Policy: LTS kernel at install; the HWE stack pulls in newer kernels over the release lifetime.
Distros.Note: The default choice. Widest hardware certification and the most search results when something goes wrong.

Distros.Name: Fedora Workstation
Distros.Policy: Tracks upstream closely and ships new kernels throughout the release. Best choice for recent hardware.
Distros.Note: Newest kernels of the mainstream options, which is what recent laptops need. Slightly more churn; expect a major upgrade about every 6 months.

Distros.Name: Pop!_OS
Distros.Policy: Ships a newer kernel than Ubuntu LTS and maintains its own hardware enablement.
Distros.Note: Ships a dedicated NVIDIA install image with the driver preinstalled - the least painful NVIDIA path there is.

Distros.Name: Debian Stable
Distros.Policy: Frozen for the life of the release (~2 years). Deliberately does not chase new hardware.
Distros.Note: Rock solid on older hardware, actively unsuitable for very recent laptops. Non-free firmware is included in the installer since Debian 12.

Distros.Name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
Distros.Policy: Rolling release - always at or near the latest stable kernel.
Distros.Note: Always-current kernel with automatic filesystem snapshots for rollback. More moving parts than a first-time user usually wants.

Distros.Name: Arch / EndeavourOS
Distros.Policy: Rolling release - latest stable kernel, often within days of release.
Distros.Note: Newest possible hardware support, at the cost of expecting you to maintain it. Not a first Linux.
